articles.title: Webinar on IoT and AI innovation in healthcare and aquaculture draws 70 participants
articles.author: Administrator
articles.body:
The IEEE Industry Applications Society (IAS) Indonesia Chapter, in collaboration with the IEEE East Java Subsection and the IEEE Northern Sumatra Subsection, held the webinar Inovasi IoT dan AI di Bidang Kesehatan dan Industri Budidaya Perikanan (Innovation of IoT and AI in Healthcare and the Aquaculture Industry) on 19 September 2026. The session ran from 09:00 to 11:00 WIB online through Zoom Meeting, and 70 participants attended.

Highlights

Prof. Ir. Khairul Anam (Universitas Jember)

The talk, Mind, Muscle, and Machine: AI-Powered Wearables untuk Gerak Manusia, began with the need for assistive technology. According to the presentation, Indonesia has 22.97 million people with disabilities, about 8.5% of the population, and a stroke prevalence of 8.3 per 1,000 people. About half of stroke survivors are said to live with long-term disability, while affordable consumer assistive devices remain scarce.

The approach rests on three research pillars of the Intelligent Systems and Robotics Lab at Universitas Jember. Bioelectric signals (EMG and EEG) are filtered, turned into features and passed to deep learning models such as CNN and LSTM, which drive the device. The first pillar is a smart prosthetic hand that recognises up to eight finger poses and predicts fingertip force in real time, with joint research reported with Friedrich-Alexander University Erlangen-Nuremberg in Germany. The second is a hand exoskeleton for stroke rehabilitation that combines game-based therapy with EMG or EEG control, and the slides mention a granted patent for a portable robot and gamification rehabilitation device.

The third pillar is a smart wheelchair that can be controlled by voice, EMG, EEG motor imagery or head motion. According to the presentation, it uses LiDAR and a Jetson Orin NX board running ROS2 for autonomous navigation, has a panic button, and reached an IoU of 0.87 and a Dice score of 0.93 in outdoor corridor segmentation tests. It was tested with cerebral palsy patients on a Careindo 503 electric wheelchair base. The speaker described all three prototypes as moving from laboratory to consumer-ready products and invited research, funding, field-test and student collaborations.

Dr. Purba Daru Kusuma, ST., MT. (Universitas Telkom)

The talk, Sistem Monitoring Kualitas Air pada Budidaya Kepiting Vertikal untuk Multi Kolam dan Multi User, presented an IoT system for crab farming in a multi-pond apartment system. The prototype was developed to monitor more than one pond and to serve more than one user, and a GSM module was added because WiFi coverage can be limited. The project aims to reach technology readiness level 6, an operational test in the field. According to the presentation, the work moved from a 2024 model under a catalyst grant with Universitas Bina Nusantara and Universitas Surabaya, to a 2025 single-pond prototype, to the 2026 multi-pond, multi-user prototype.

The hardware measures pH, temperature and salinity and sends the data over GSM to a web server at krabcare.com. The slides report a laboratory test on 12 September 2026 at the Rnest laboratory of Universitas Telkom with three testers from Politeknik Negeri Bandung, covering software function, usability and hardware accuracy. The pH sensor had an average error below 2% at pH 4.01 and 9.1, the temperature sensor below 7%, and the salinity sensor about 5% at 0.4 g per 100 mL. Readings were weaker at some points, for example pH 3, temperatures near 13 degrees Celsius, and very low or higher salinity solutions.

On the software side, the slides note that predictions for 15 to 30 minutes ahead had very small error, while 60-minute predictions had large error, and the overall usability score was 4.7. The next steps named in the presentation are to finalise the prototype from the laboratory results, run a field test at aquaculture ponds in Surabaya, and revise the outputs.

Attendance and feedback

The participants were mostly university students and lecturers, with a smaller group from the general public. They came from universities and a few other organisations in many parts of Indonesia, from Sumatra and Java to Madura and Maluku, and most were not yet IEEE members. The main reasons for joining were to learn the basics of IoT, to understand how AI is used in industry, to find references for study and research, to follow current technology trends and to learn more about the Chapter and the two Subsections.

Next steps

The Chapter will announce future activities through its usual channels, including the Chapter Instagram account at https://instagram.com/ieeeiasindonesiachapter.

articles.title: Webinar on IoT and AI for community welfare presents fleet management, rural energy and IoT training
articles.author: Administrator
articles.body:
The IEEE Industry Applications Society (IAS) Indonesia Chapter, in collaboration with the IEEE East Java Subsection and the IEEE Northern Sumatra Subsection, held the Webinar Pemanfaatan IoT dan Kecerdasan Buatan bagi Kesejahteraan Masyarakat (the use of IoT and artificial intelligence for community welfare) on Saturday, 22 August 2026, from 15:30 to 17:00 WIB. The session took place online via Zoom Meeting, and 50 participants attended.

Three speakers from industry and academia showed how the Internet of Things (IoT) and related technologies can serve logistics, rural communities and education.

Highlights

OSLOG: digital fleet management and logistics

Handy Madinata, S.TI. (Founder and CEO, PT. iSense Technology; PT Integrasia Utama) presented OSLOG Datatec, a platform for fleet management and logistics. He described common problems: fleets that cannot be tracked in real time, rising fuel and maintenance costs, driver behaviour that is hard to measure, and proof of delivery still done by hand.

According to the presentation, the platform combines telematics, cloud computing, data analytics and safety sensors around three elements: vehicle, driver and operation. It records braking, stopping, lane changes, turning at intersections and overall ride comfort, and turns these data into a driver score, a driver ranking and a risk analysis that support safety coaching. Other features include route planning, electronic proof of delivery, driver fatigue monitoring and a digital audit trail of fleet activity.

Smart power electronics for rural and coastal energy independence

Prof. Aripriharta, S.T., M.T., PhD. (Universitas Negeri Malang) argued that electricity is now almost everywhere in Indonesia but still comes mostly from fossil fuel. The slides cite a 99.83% electrification ratio, a fossil share of 83.7% in power generation in 2025, and 12,968 coastal villages. Rural and coastal areas have strong solar, wind and water resources, but fluctuating supply makes conventional systems fragile.

His answer is smart power electronics: converters with intelligent control that keep voltage stable and extract maximum power. The slides present a swarm-intelligence maximum power point tracking method and report efficiency of 95.0 to 99.1% against about 34% for a conventional algorithm under shading. He proposed micro-grids of 500 W to 1 kW built on three pillars: solar panels, a small vertical-axis wind turbine for coastal sites, and pico-hydro with an Archimedes screw for irrigation channels. According to the slides, levelised cost is about Rp 740 per kWh for solar and about Rp 489 per kWh for pico-hydro in the simulation, against a non-subsidised grid tariff of Rp 1,444.70 to Rp 1,501 per kWh, with payback in two to four years. Field examples from East Java included street lights, a 5 kWp system at a boarding school, wind turbines for a coffee stall and pico-hydro units.

SEMOTE-G: an IoT trainer for education

Dr. Ir. Made Santo Gitakarma, S.T., M.T., MCE. (Universitas Pendidikan Ganesha) introduced the Smart Environmental Monitoring Trainer for Education - Ganesha (SEMOTE-G). He began with the basics of IoT, its six building blocks and common communication protocols.

The trainer uses a NodeMCU ESP8266 microcontroller with temperature and humidity, air pressure, light and distance sensors. It sends readings as JSON messages over MQTT, a lightweight publish and subscribe protocol, to a Mosquitto broker on a Raspberry Pi 4. Node-RED on the same Raspberry Pi then processes the data and shows it on a web dashboard with gauges and charts. The whole system runs on a local network, which, according to the presentation, keeps data private and independent of the public internet.

Attendance and feedback

The audience was diverse. Most participants were university students and lecturers, from undergraduate to doctoral level, joined by researchers, industry professionals and small business owners. They connected from universities and institutions across Java, Sumatra, Bali, Nusa Tenggara and Kalimantan. Their main reasons for joining were to learn IoT basics, to understand AI in industry and to follow technology trends.

Next steps

Announcements of future Chapter webinars are posted on the Chapter's Instagram account.

articles.title: IAS Webinar on IoT and AI technology draws  83 participants from accross the country
articles.author: Administrator
articles.body:
The IEEE Industry Applications Society (IAS) Indonesia Chapter, in collaboration with the IEEE East Java Subsection and the IEEE Northern Sumatra Subsection, held the Webinar IoT dan Teknologi AI on Saturday, 18 July 2026, from 15:30 to 17:00 WIB. The session took place online via Zoom Meeting, and 83 participants completed the attendance and evaluation form.

Speakers from industry and academia presented applications of the Internet of Things (IoT) and artificial intelligence (AI) in industrial safety, agriculture, and heart disease diagnosis.

Highlights

Productivity, safety and security in industry with AI, IoT and compression

Mauritz Panggabean, PhD (AssistX), Chief Scientific Officer of AssistX, presented the products and solutions of this Indonesian research-based technology company, which was established in 2018. The talk focused on two areas. The first is computer vision for CCTV surveillance: an edge device compresses live video streams, reported as more than 90% more efficient with an average SSIM (structural similarity) of 0.987, while AI analytics such as people counting, intrusion detection and tamper detection run on the compressed streams. The second is intelligent document processing, which uses generative AI and vision AI to classify documents and extract data from ID cards, CVs and bank statements.

According to the presentation, one banking client monitoring more than 6,000 ATMs and branch offices reduced its response time to potential fraud incidents from one to two weeks to 10 to 15 minutes. A defence-sector client raised document processing from up to 250,000 to more than 6 million documents per year, about 24 times faster.

Agricultural mechanization with automatic tractor control

Dr. Purba Daru Kusuma (Universitas Telkom) described an IoT-based monitoring system for agricultural machinery, developed for the UPTD BP Mektan agricultural mechanization unit in West Java. He identified three problems: rental records kept by hand, no way to see where machines are, and no reliable record of whether a machine is working or idle.

The proposed design uses GPS and voltage and current sensors on the machine battery, an ESP32 microcontroller that formats the readings, a cellular module that sends them to a server, and a web dashboard showing asset location and status. The benefits presented were real-time monitoring, accurate operating-hour logs and better management of regional assets.

Artificial intelligence and heart health

Riandini, S.T., M.Sc. (Politeknik Negeri Jakarta) explained why AI suits cardiology: almost every heart examination produces digital data, including ECG, echocardiography, CT and MRI. She reviewed how deep learning is used in each modality and used myocardial scar segmentation on cardiac MRI as a case study, with U-Net based networks as the main architecture family.

She also raised the challenges of generalising models to data from other hospitals, and stressed that AI supports doctors rather than replaces them (human-in-the-loop). Trends she listed include foundation models, federated learning, explainable AI and digital twins. Clinical use still needs external validation, interpretability, safety and close collaboration between computer scientists, doctors and regulators.

Attendance and feedback

The audience was diverse. Most participants were university students and lecturers, ranging from undergraduate to doctoral level, joined by professionals from industry and other organisations. They came from universities, a polytechnic, a higher education service office and private companies in cities across Sumatra, Java, Sulawesi and Nusa Tenggara.

Their interests were just as varied. Participants named industrial automation, healthcare and biomedical engineering, power systems, telecommunications, renewable energy, education and robotics among the topics they wish to see next, which shows how widely IoT and AI now reach across fields.

Overall satisfaction averaged 4.71 out of 5: 62 participants gave 5, 18 gave 4 and 3 gave 3. Participants also rated four aspects of the webinar:

  • Speaker delivery: 79 of 83 rated it good or very good (45 very good).
  • Audio and visual quality: 76 rated it good or very good, and 7 rated it fair.
  • Depth of material: 76 rated it good or very good, 6 fair and 1 poor.
  • Relevance to their needs: 76 rated it good or very good, 6 fair and 1 poor.

When asked whether they would join a future webinar, 42 participants (51%) said they would definitely attend, 40 (48%) answered maybe, depending on the topic, and 1 said no.

Suggestions for future topics

Participants asked for more on AI in industrial automation and manufacturing, machine learning and deep learning, and AI in healthcare and biomedical engineering. Other topics mentioned were cyber security, renewable energy, natural language processing, robotics and AI in education. Two participants asked for a short live demonstration, and one suggested a later start time.

Next steps

The topics and comments above are a useful guide for future Chapter webinars. Follow the Chapter on Instagram for announcements.

articles.title: Webinar on IoT and information technology brings together four speakers and student participants
articles.author: Administrator
articles.body:
The IEEE Industry Applications Society (IAS) Indonesia Chapter held the online Webinar IoT dan Teknologi Informasi (IoT and Information Technology Webinar) on Saturday, 13 December 2025, from 09:00 to 10:30 WIB via Zoom. Four lecturers from four Indonesian universities presented. Participants came from 12 institutions across several cities, and included students, lecturers and school teachers.

Highlights

The Chapter invited four speakers, each presenting a topic within their own field:

  • Prof. Dr. Ir. Fahmi, S.T., M.Sc., IPM (Universitas Sumatera Utara): Smart Garbage Electric Vehicle, Solusi transport sampah cerdas berbasis EV
  • Muhammad Yazid, B.Eng., M.Eng. (Institut Teknologi Sepuluh Nopember): Algoritma Data Security untuk Perangkat IoT
  • Erwin Sutanto, S.T., M.Sc. (Universitas Airlangga): Residual Current Monitor Application with Fiber Optic
  • Dr. Purba Daru Kusuma (Telkom University): Collaborative Online Learning System

The session on data security for IoT devices was based on the paper "Simple authentication method for vehicle monitoring IoT device with verifiable data integrity", published in IEEE Internet of Things Journal in 2022. It looked at vehicle monitoring, where devices transmit data while moving and network quality changes constantly. The talk set out three security requirements: mutual authentication between device and server, integrity of the data stored in the server database, and anonymity of the device during transmission.

The presentation then explained why several common approaches are a poor fit for low-power hardware. Public key encryption is computationally expensive, and static shared keys allow a device to be cloned once the key is extracted. Pools of shadow identifiers use scarce device memory, and a trusted gateway becomes a single point of failure. As an alternative, the speaker described a protocol based on symmetric encryption and parallel hash chains. The talk covered the initialization phase, the handshake between device and server, and the handling of transmission failures. It closed with security and performance analyses of communication and computational cost.

[[IMAGE: screenshot of the Zoom session showing the speakers and participants | Speakers and participants during the IoT and Information Technology Webinar on Zoom]]

Participation

The webinar drew a varied audience. Participants came from 12 institutions, mostly universities plus one vocational high school. Telkom University, Institut Teknologi Sepuluh Nopember (ITS) and Universitas Negeri Malang were the largest groups. Other institutions represented were Universitas Muhammadiyah Ponorogo, Universitas Jember, Universitas Logistik dan Bisnis Internasional, Universitas NU Sidoarjo, Binus University, Universitas Brawijaya, Universitas Airlangga, UMKT and SMK Negeri 2 Pontianak.

Geographically, participants joined from several cities in Java, including Surabaya, Malang, Ponorogo, Jember, Sidoarjo and Bandung, and from Pontianak in West Kalimantan. Participants included students at undergraduate and graduate level, university lecturers and academic staff, and a vocational school teacher. Both state and private institutions took part, and the participants' fields ranged from engineering, science and computing to other disciplines such as nutrition.

The session ran on schedule and without disruption. A certificate of attendance was sent by email to participants after the webinar.

Next steps

The Chapter plans to continue organising activities on industry applications topics for students, lecturers and practitioners.

articles.title: IEEE Industry Applications Society Indonesia Chapter is officially formed
articles.author: Administrator
articles.summary: IEEE has approved the formation of the IEEE Industry Applications Society Indonesia Chapter, effective 10 September 2025, to connect engineers and researchers working on industrial technology.
articles.body:
The IEEE Industry Applications Society (IAS) Indonesia Chapter has been formally established under the IEEE Indonesia Section. IEEE approved the Chapter with an effective formation date of 10 September 2025, giving engineers, researchers and industry practitioners in Indonesia a dedicated community for the industrial applications of electrical and electronic technologies.

Approval by IEEE

On 15 September 2025, Cecelia Jankowski, Managing Director of IEEE Member and Geographic Activities, confirmed that the requirements of the MGA Board Operations Manual had been met and that the Chapter had been formed. The letter was copied to IEEE Region 10 leadership, the IAS President and staff, and the IEEE Indonesia Section Chair.

Why the Chapter was formed

Indonesia needs to expand and modernize its industrial capacity to sustain economic growth, and much of its industrial output still depends on manual or semi-automated processes. Technologies such as the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI) and advanced automation can improve efficiency and support real-time decision-making, but using them well requires collaboration, research and knowledge sharing. The Chapter aims to provide a platform where researchers, professionals and policymakers can connect, exchange ideas and support workforce development.

Founding members and officers

The Chapter began with a petition from IEEE IAS members of diverse backgrounds and institutional affiliations, spread across Indonesia from North Sumatra to West Java, East Java and Bali. Their institutions include Institut Teknologi Sepuluh Nopember, Universitas Sumatera Utara, Universitas Airlangga, Institut Teknologi Bandung, Universitas Negeri Surabaya, Universitas Negeri Malang, Universitas Pendidikan Ganesha and Universitas Telkom.

The Chapter's officers for 2026 are:

  • Chapter Chair: Muhammad Yazid (Institut Teknologi Sepuluh Nopember)
  • Chapter Vice Chair: Fahmi Fahmi (Universitas Sumatera Utara)
  • Chapter Secretary: Purba Daru Kusuma (Universitas Telkom) and Erwin Sutanto (Universitas Airlangga)
  • Chapter Treasurer: Pradini Puspitaningayu (Universitas Negeri Surabaya)
